questions.question: Which of these is the most testable success criterion for an email-classification prompt?
options: The model should classify emails well
Category matches the human label on at least 18 of 20 test emails
Outputs should feel accurate to the team
The prompt should be as detailed as possible
questions.explanation: A testable criterion is measurable against a labelled test set; the others are vague or describe the prompt rather than the output.

questions.question: Your prompt scores 15/20. You add an example, reword two rules and reorder the sections, and it now scores 18/20. What is the main problem?
options: Three points is not a meaningful improvement
You should have used LLM-as-judge instead
You cannot tell which change helped, and one may have broken another case
questions.explanation: Changing one thing at a time lets you attribute improvements and spot changes that silently cause regressions.

questions.question: Which is a known caveat of LLM-as-judge grading?
options: Judges may favour longer or more confident answers, so their scores should be spot-checked against human grades
Judges always agree perfectly with human reviewers
Judges are the best way to verify numeric totals
questions.explanation: LLM judges can be biased by length, confidence or ordering; validate them on a sample and use code checks for verifiable facts.

questions.question: Before switching your production prompt to a newer model, what should you do?
options: Nothing; newer models are always better on every input
Test it only on the cases that failed before
Rerun the full versioned test set as a regression check
questions.explanation: Any change, including a model switch, can break previously passing cases, so the full suite should be rerun.
